observations: Neet has connected full narrow trunk, fine four supported legs, visible neck and broad cupped ears. Buddy has a continuous elongated trunk and credible clearance; far foreleg overlaps near foreleg, with a small distinct far paw visible. No detached or additional limbs.

Buddy retains irregular outward/downward moustache, small under-chin furnishing and hanging ears. However repeated meandering engraved lines fill his flank and thigh, and short pointed tufts rise at the neck. Neet also retains wavy directional marks across flank/shoulder and a visibly tufted upright nub. These are drawn coat strands rather than random pigment grain.

Blue sock remains held in Buddy mouth; couch is behind him, Neet confronts the vacuum, and the stored cord establishes the machine has not yet been plugged in. Compatible with Act II anchor. Opposing intentions are readily legible. Room perspective, floor contact and cropped hand are coherent; human appearance remains provisional.

Neet low forward stance connects head/neck/chest/ribcage/pelvis to four supported fine limbs. Buddy has a continuous foreshortened torso and clear substantial legs; one front limb is naturally partly hidden by the machine. Cord remains separate from feet. No material support or limb-ownership fault found.

Neet flank, shoulder and neck carry conspicuous repeated curved/engraved hair strokes, with a fringed throat/underbody. Buddy has directional shoulder/chest hair and a brush-like tail edge. This is actual coat rendering rather than watercolor paper grain; prior acceptance does not close the current short-coat requirement.

Kitchen cabinets, bowl, ordinary corded appliance and cropped operating hand match the scene. Neet confronts the nozzle and Buddy stands behind it near the slack cord without contact. The additional Cheerio is compatible with crumb defense and does not need to be the already eaten Cheerio. His open mouth reads as comic protest; scene adds the active confrontation between setup and aftermath.

Both dogs have continuous spines/trunks, visible necks and credible limb roots. Four Neet feet and four Buddy feet are assigned coherently and grounded. Buddy maintains torso length, substantial legs and clearance. No disconnected anatomy or impossible support found.

Buddy muzzle has irregular short pale moustache ends and a modest under-chin beard; no need to enlarge these. Ear and paw furnishings are regional. His neck, shoulder, torso and upper legs still show tapered hair strokes, and a raised spiky contour runs behind the ears onto the upper back. Neet has lighter repeated directional body marks and a raised tuft-like nub. Smooth broad shading has improved the image but has not removed strand texture.

Neet stands at the end of the muddy trail, with the rightmost rear foot still at/on the rug edge; Buddy stops on clean wood and looks down. Actual prose says Neet returned across the rug and Buddy stopped at the edge, without an all-paws-off requirement. This is compatible with that anchor and is not a narrative defect. Rug remains flat before Heather lifts it; no premature breakfast or returned vacuum appears. Cropped human legs are provisional.
The quiet proud Neet versus downward-looking Buddy provides a distinct reversal and readable payoff. Sunlit room, door, rug perspective and shadows are coherent.
